text:
Anthony Cirelli is the kind of player whose box score undersells him, and this season it's undersold him more than usual. He has 11 points in 17 games, a decent pace, but Tampa Bay has scored 7.6 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. That's one of the bigger gaps in the league, and it's the kind that usually swings back.

The process is all there. The Lightning have controlled 59.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five-on-five with him out there, and he's had a hot stretch lately, eight points in his last ten games. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 95th percentile of forwards last season, with the caveat that he skates with excellent linemates.

He's 29 now, a two-time Cup winner and a 72nd overall pick who turned into one of the league's best two-way centers. His own shooting, 17.9%, is a touch high, so expect fewer goals of his own and more assists as the on-ice luck evens out. Our range puts him around 55 points by April.
headline: Anthony Cirelli is better than his line looks
